description: Well-documented, real per-company data points found during research that are not covered by the 27 official survey questions but could plausibly matter to a values-driven investor. Logged here for review -- NOT added to the official question set. Each entry: a proposed survey question in the same plain-language 1-5-importance style, the supporting data source, and current coverage.

candidates.proposed_question: Prioritizing companies with a validated Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) emissions-reduction commitment
candidates.rationale: SBTi validation is a much stronger, independently-verified signal of real decarbonization commitment than the 10-K keyword scan used for Q1/Q2, which only detects whether a company *mentions* climate/renewable topics in its business description, not whether it has a validated target.
candidates.coverage_status: Source confirmed reachable from this environment (HTTP 200) but not yet integrated into the collection pipeline -- see logs/suggested_sources.md. 0 companies currently checked.
candidates.confidence_if_implemented: High (SBTi validation status is a binary, independently-audited fact)

candidates.proposed_question: Prioritizing companies recognized in JUST Capital's annual worker-treatment rankings
candidates.rationale: JUST Capital publishes an independently-compiled worker-treatment ranking across large-cap US companies, which would materially strengthen Q5 (fair wages)/Q7 (DEI)/Q8 (worker safety) beyond the current 10-K keyword scan and OSHA name-match.

candidates.rationale: A common values-investing screen (comparable in spirit to founder_led/family_owned in Q24) that the official 27-question list does not cover. Implemented and populated for all 503 companies as the `women_led` field -- see schema/company_schema.json's `additional_criteria` section for the field's data dictionary entry.
candidates.source: DEF 14A proxy statement (EDGAR) -- see find_ceo_gender_signal() in scripts/lib.py
candidates.coverage_status: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20 via scripts/fix_women_led.py, run across all 503 companies. Identifies the CEO's surname via a name+title-adjacency regex, then reads the filing's own honorific (Mr./Ms./Mrs.) or, failing that, a majority of pronoun references (she/her vs he/his) for that specific named person -- never guessed from a first name. Tested against ~30 known-CEO tickers (Mary Barra/GM, Lisa Su/AMD, Carol Tome/UPS, Vicki Hollub/OXY, Gail Boudreaux/ELV, Kecia Steelman/ULTA as True cases; Tim Cook/AAPL, Satya Nadella/MSFT, Jamie Dimon/JPM, and others as False cases) with no observed misattribution after iterating out several false-positive modes (compensation-table jargon like "NEO" being mis-read as a surname, all-caps document headers splitting vote counts from the same properly-cased name, a single incidental past-tense CEO-title mention elsewhere in the document out-voting the real CEO on a 1-1 tie). See coverage numbers in README.md.
candidates.confidence_if_implemented: Low (flattened-text regex heuristic reading the filing's own gendered language -- same class of caveat as founder_led/family_owned, not a verified/audited fact)
